apply.name: apply
apply.help:
USAGE
  ht apply [options] [plugins...]

Resolve a plugin's dependency graph and materialize it

ARGUMENTS
  [plugins]  Plugins to apply

EXAMPLES
  ht apply base
  ht apply base --harness claude-code
  ht apply work --global
  ht apply ./build/my-pkg
  ht apply base --format json
  ht apply base --on-conflict replace

OPTIONS
  --global                  Materialize into machine home instead of the project
  --project <path>          Project directory
  --harness <slugs>         Comma-separated harness slugs
  --all                     Install/apply every canonical HT-mapped target (not agent-skills)
  --dry-run                 Show what would be written
  --format <mode>           Output format: human or json
  --interactive             Prompt instead of relying on explicit flags
  --ignore-plugin-versions  Skip checking Claude plugin pins against installed versions
  --strict-plugin-versions  Fail apply (exit 2) if any pinned plugin violates its version constraint
  --sync-plugins            Refresh all pinned plugin resources from install trees before apply (unresolved plugins are synced by default)
  --on-conflict <policy>    What to do when it already exists: replace, skip, prompt or cancel. overwrite, ignore and fail are aliases. Non-interactive default: cancel
  --explain                 Print the resolution trail: selected versions with their constraints, and every resource decision
  --update                  Ignore apm.lock.yaml, re-resolve the dependency graph, and refresh file hashes
  --strict                  Fail apply when ${VAR} environment placeholders cannot be resolved
  --force                   Override critical hidden-Unicode findings and continue apply
  -y, --yes                 Install pinned marketplace plugins without a prompt
  --force-remove            Also remove managed files you changed and unmanaged files in the way

apply.name: install
apply.help:
USAGE
  ht install [options]

Onboard a project from apm.yml (same as apply with no plugin selector)

Reads repo-root apm.yml, resolves dependencies.apm (including transitive dependencies.apm on fetched packages) / dependencies.mcp (including MCP Registry v0.1 identities such as io.github...), compiles local .apm/ primitives, writes apm.lock.yaml, and materializes resolved target harness directories. Registry strings are fetched from registry.modelcontextprotocol.io and converted to the same native MCP files HT already emits. Self-defined registry: false entries keep command/url as authored. --mcp <id> appends the identity to apm.yml then runs install; a failed install rolls the manifest write back. Target resolution: --target/--all/--harness, then targets: in apm.yml, then project/global harness preference, then filesystem auto-detect. Declared targets: win over preference and folder detection. Fails closed when no target can be resolved. Commit the lockfile plus generated harness output. Same project-scope flags as apply. Does not take a plugin selector or --global.

EXAMPLES
  ht install
  ht install --project .
  ht install --mcp io.github.github/github-mcp-server --target cursor
  ht install --target cursor,claude
  ht install --harness claude-code,cursor
  ht install --dry-run
  ht install --update

OPTIONS
  --project <path>          Project directory
  --harness <slugs>         Comma-separated harness slugs
  --all                     Install/apply every canonical HT-mapped target (not agent-skills)
  --dry-run                 Show what would be written
  --format <mode>           Output format: human or json
  --interactive             Prompt instead of relying on explicit flags
  --ignore-plugin-versions  Skip checking Claude plugin pins against installed versions
  --strict-plugin-versions  Fail apply (exit 2) if any pinned plugin violates its version constraint
  --sync-plugins            Refresh all pinned plugin resources from install trees before apply (unresolved plugins are synced by default)
  --on-conflict <policy>    What to do when it already exists: replace, skip, prompt or cancel. overwrite, ignore and fail are aliases. Non-interactive default: cancel
  --explain                 Print the resolution trail: selected versions with their constraints, and every resource decision
  --update                  Ignore apm.lock.yaml, re-resolve the dependency graph, and refresh file hashes
  --strict                  Fail apply when ${VAR} environment placeholders cannot be resolved
  --force                   Override critical hidden-Unicode findings and continue apply
  -y, --yes                 Install pinned marketplace plugins without a prompt
  --force-remove            Also remove managed files you changed and unmanaged files in the way
  --mcp <id>                Append an MCP Registry v0.1 identity to apm.yml dependencies.mcp, then install

  --all             Approve all currently pending packages
  --recommended     Approve the org executables.recommend set
  --list            Show effective trust decision per installed package
  --format <mode>   Output format: human or json

audit.name: audit
audit.help:
USAGE
  ht audit [options]

Scan a project for hidden Unicode, lockfile hashes, apm-policy.yml, and executable trust

Default scan covers lockfile-recorded deployed files plus local primitive dirs, and evaluates apm-policy.yml when present. --ci fails on critical Unicode, hash mismatch/extra/missing, blocking policy, or required-executable-untrusted. --require-policy with --ci fails if no policy file exists. --strip removes critical and warning characters (mutually exclusive with --ci). Use --file to scan any one file.

EXAMPLES
  ht audit
  ht audit --file .cursorrules
  ht audit --ci --require-policy --format json
  ht audit --strip --dry-run

OPTIONS
  --project <path>  Project directory
  --file <path>     Scan a single file instead of the project
  --ci              CI gate: fail on critical Unicode, lockfile hash drift, policy, or untrusted required executables
  --policy <path>   Policy file (default: apm-policy.yml at project root)
  --require-policy  With --ci, fail if no policy file is present
  --strip           Remove critical and warning hidden-Unicode characters
  --dry-run         Preview --strip without writing
  --format <mode>   Output format: human or json

  ht compile --all
  ht compile --project . --format json

commands.name: sync
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht harness sync [options]

Union resources from registered harnesses and materialize with last-write conflicts

Scans every registered harness, unions portable types (skills, MCP, rules, host plugin install trees, and other serializer-supported resources), keeps the newest on-disk copy when the same identity differs (later registered harness on ties), and emits shared skill paths when multiple targets can read them. Claude and Cursor plugin trees are copied into each native root (they do not share a runtime plugin directory). Skills, agents, and commands inside those plugins are also materialized into `.agents` (and equivalent folders) for OpenCode and other harnesses that do not load Cursor/Claude plugin roots. Matching CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md share one file: AGENTS.md is canonical and CLAUDE.md links to it unless copy mode is set. Configure with `harnessSync.pluginResources` in config.jsonc (`symlink`, `copy`, or `clone`) or `--plugin-resources`. Default scope is the home directory. This is not copy-from-one-harness mirror.

EXAMPLES
  ht harness sync
  ht harness sync --dry-run --format json
  ht harness sync --plugin-resources copy
  ht harness sync --project .

OPTIONS
  --project <path>           Sync a git-backed project instead of home
  --dry-run                  Show what would be written without writing files
  --plugin-resources <mode>  How to materialize Cursor/Claude plugin files into .agents: symlink, copy, or clone (default symlink, or harnessSync.pluginResources in config.jsonc)
  --format <mode>            Output format: human or json

USAGE
  ht lock export [options]

Export a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM inventory from the existing lockfile (no re-resolve)

Inventory export only: reads apm.lock.yaml and serializes it. Never re-resolves, re-hashes, or touches the network. Default format is CycloneDX 1.5; --format spdx writes SPDX 2.3. This is not a security attestation: the document is unsigned and does not claim SLSA. --timestamp pins the document time; otherwise SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, then the lockfile generated_at. Diagnostics go to stderr so stdout stays pipe-clean.

EXAMPLES
  ht lock export
  ht lock export --format cyclonedx -o sbom.json
  ht lock export --format spdx --timestamp 2024-06-01T00:00:00+00:00
  ht lock export --project .

OPTIONS
  -f, --format <format>  SBOM output format: cyclonedx (1.5) or spdx (2.3)
  -o, --output <file>    Write the SBOM to a file instead of stdout
  --project <path>       Project directory
  -g, --global           Read apm.lock.yaml from ~/.harnesstap/
  --timestamp <ts>       Pin the SBOM timestamp (timezone-aware ISO 8601) for reproducible output

  ht profile file-diff [options] <name>

Show live content vs after-apply (profile) as a unified diff

ARGUMENTS
  <name>  Profile plugin name or selector

EXAMPLES
  ht profile file-diff work --path .claude/skills/foo/SKILL.md --scope home
  ht profile file-diff work --path .claude/skills/foo/SKILL.md --scope home --format json

OPTIONS
  --path <path>           Managed relative path
  --format <mode>         Output format: human or json
  --no-interactive        Disable interactive prompts
  --scope <home|project>  home or project
  --project <path>        Project path (required when --scope project)
  --harness <slug>        Harness slug

project.name: scan
project.help:
USAGE
  ht scan [options] [path]

Scan a project directory or plugin source and import configurations into the database

ARGUMENTS
  [path]  Project directory or plugin source to scan

EXAMPLES
  ht scan
  ht scan ./my-project --dry-run
  ht scan --harness claude-code
  ht scan --format json

OPTIONS
  --harness <slugs>   Harness slug(s): scan filter, or install targets with --global
  --dry-run           Show what would be imported without writing to DB
  --global            Install imported plugin sources into global harness locations
  --overwrite         Overwrite library resources when scan content differs
  --skip-existing     Keep existing library resources when scan content differs
  --namespace <name>  Namespace for imported project resources
  --format <mode>     Output format: human or json

project.name: use
project.help:
USAGE
  ht use [options]

Switch to a project-configured profile and environment

EXAMPLES
  ht use
  ht use --profile dev
  ht use --list
  ht use --profile dev --dry-run --format json

OPTIONS
  --profile <name>        Profile key from apm.yml
  --project <path>        Project directory
  --list                  List profiles from project config without applying
  --dry-run               Show what would be written without applying
  --force                 Apply even when the profile is already active and in sync
  --no-pull               Do not auto-pull missing published plugin dependencies
  --harness <slugs>       Comma-separated harness slugs (defaults to global harness preference)
  --account <name>        Cloud account name for dependency pulls
  --base-url <url>        Cloud base URL for dependency pulls
  --on-conflict <policy>  What to do when it already exists: replace, skip, prompt or cancel. overwrite, ignore and fail are aliases. Non-interactive default: cancel
  --no-interactive        Disable interactive prompts
  --format <mode>         Output format: human or json

project.name: mirror
project.help:
USAGE
  ht mirror [options] [path]

Rematerialize registered harness files from one on-disk harness (or plugin/AGENTS.md fallback)

ARGUMENTS
  [path]  Project directory

EXAMPLES
  ht mirror
  ht mirror . --dry-run
  ht mirror --reference auto --format json

OPTIONS
  --dry-run                       Show what would be written without writing files
  --from <slug>                   On-disk harness to copy from (same as --force-shift-reference)
  --force-shift-reference <slug>  Deprecated alias of --from
  --reference <strategy>          Reference source: disk, plugin, agents, or auto (main is a deprecated alias of disk)
  --format <mode>                 Output format: human or json

project.name: history
project.help:
USAGE
  ht history [options] [path]

List configuration snapshots for a project

ARGUMENTS
  [path]  Project directory

EXAMPLES
  ht history
  ht history --format json
  ht history --show-id

OPTIONS
  --format <mode>  Output format: human or json
  --show-id        Show snapshot IDs in human-readable tables

project.name: revert
project.help:
USAGE
  ht revert [options] [snapshot-id]

Revert a project or global apply snapshot

ARGUMENTS
  [snapshot-id]  Snapshot ID to revert to

EXAMPLES
  ht revert <snapshot-id>
  ht revert <snapshot-id> --dry-run

OPTIONS
  --dry-run        Show what would be restored without writing
  --force-remove   Remove files even when they were changed or not made by HarnessTap
  --format <mode>  Output format: human or json

project.name: status
project.help:
USAGE
  ht status [options] [path]

Show current project status and drift summary

ARGUMENTS
  [path]  Project directory

EXAMPLES
  ht status
  ht status --check
  ht status --format json

OPTIONS
  --format <mode>  Output format: human or json
  --check          Exit with code 1 when snapshot or lock drift exists

resource.name: resource
resource.help:
USAGE
  ht resource [options] [command]

Manage resources (individual pieces of AI configuration like agents, skills, or instructions)

COMMANDS
  list (ls) [type]   List imported resources, optionally filtered by type or search
  show [resource]    Show a resource by name, selector, or ULID
  sync [selector]    Sync plugin resources and marketplace-linked definitions from install trees
  delete [resource]  Delete a resource from the library
  scope <name>       Add harnesses to a resource's scope
  directories        Manage directories scanned into the resource library

commands.name: list
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht resource list [options] [type]

List imported resources, optionally filtered by type or search

ARGUMENTS
  [type]  Filter by resource type (instruction, skill, rule, mcp_server, permission, hook, agent, command, env_var, model_config, plugin)

EXAMPLES
  ht resource list
  ht resource list skill
  ht resource list --search caveman

OPTIONS
  -s, --search <query>  Search by name or description (skips interactive filter)
  --format <mode>       Output format: human or json
  --show-id             Show IDs in human-readable tables
  --all                 Show all resources per type (default: first 10 per type)

commands.name: show
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht resource show [options] [resource]

Show a resource by name, selector, or ULID

ARGUMENTS
  <resource>  Resource name or ID

EXAMPLES
  ht resource show caveman
  ht resource show skill:caveman --format json
  ht resource show tiny-skill --full

OPTIONS
  --format <mode>  Output format: human or json
  --show-id        Show IDs in list-oriented human tables
  --all-fields     Show all resource metadata fields
  --full           Show the full resource body instead of a truncated preview
  --interactive    Prompt instead of relying on explicit flags

commands.name: sync
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht resource sync [options] [selector]

Sync plugin resources and marketplace-linked definitions from install trees

ARGUMENTS
  [selector]  Linked resource selector (optional)

EXAMPLES
  ht resource sync
  ht resource sync plugin:my-plugin --dry-run
  ht resource sync --on-conflict replace

OPTIONS
  --overwrite             Overwrite cached definitions when install tree differs
  --on-conflict <policy>  What to do when it already exists: replace, skip, prompt or cancel. overwrite, ignore and fail are aliases
  --force                 Sync pinned resources
  --dry-run               Report linked resources without writing changes
  --check                 Exit 1 when any linked resource is stale
  --force-remove          Back up and replace files in a host plugin cache folder that HarnessTap did not write
  --format <mode>         Output format: human or json

commands.name: delete
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht resource delete [options] [resource]

Delete a resource from the library

ARGUMENTS
  <resource>  Resource name or ID

EXAMPLES
  ht resource delete caveman
  ht resource delete

OPTIONS
  -s, --search <query>  Filter resources in the delete wizard
  --interactive         Prompt instead of relying on explicit flags
  --format <mode>       Output format: human or json

commands.name: scope
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht resource scope [options] <name>

Add harnesses to a resource's scope

ARGUMENTS

EXAMPLES
  ht resource scope filesystem --add cursor,codex

OPTIONS
  --add <harnesses>  Comma-separated harness ids to add to this resource's scope
  --format <mode>    Output format: human or json

commands.name: directories
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht resource directories [options] [command]

Manage directories scanned into the resource library

COMMANDS
  list (ls)           List directories tracked for resource import
  add <path>          Track a directory and import resources (skip existing)
  remove (rm) <path>  Stop tracking a directory (library resources stay)
  rescan              Re-scan home defaults and every tracked directory

commands.name: list
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht resource directories list [options]

List directories tracked for resource import

EXAMPLES
  ht resource directories list
  ht resource directories list --format json

OPTIONS
  --format <mode>  Output format: human or json

commands.name: add
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht resource directories add [options] <path>

Track a directory and import resources (skip existing)

ARGUMENTS

EXAMPLES

  ht resource directories add ./my-project --format json

OPTIONS
  --format <mode>  Output format: human or json

commands.name: remove
commands.help:
USAGE
  ht resource directories remove [options] <path>

Stop tracking a directory (library resources stay)

ARGUMENTS
  <path>  Tracked directory to stop watching

EXAMPLES

  ht resource directories rm ./my-project --format json

OPTIONS
  --format <mode>  Output format: human or json

commands.name: rescan
commands.help:

  ht resource directories rescan [options]

Re-scan home defaults and every tracked directory

EXAMPLES
  ht resource directories rescan
  ht resource directories rescan --format json

OPTIONS
  --format <mode>  Output format: human or json
